steps.what: 1. RewardsSet.WithRewardsFromRoom -> GenerateRewardsFor (list construction, BEFORE GenerateWithoutOffering is ever called): Monster adds GoldReward(construct only) then RollForPotionAndAddTo (the ONE real draw in this step -- PotionRewardOdds.Roll, on player.PlayerOdds.PotionReward's own Rng) then CardReward(construct only); Elite is the same plus a trailing RelicReward(construct only); Boss is Gold+Potion-roll+Card with NO relic; the final act's Boss returns before any of this runs at all (RewardsSet.cs:85-91, 206-256).
steps.rationale: generate_combat_rewards (rewards.py) reproduces the exact draw: `got_potion = run.potion_reward_odds.roll(room_type, force=force)` runs FIRST, strictly before the gold draw, matching that RollForPotionAndAddTo is called before GenerateWithoutOffering's populate loop ever reaches GoldReward.Populate -- verified by reading PotionRewardOdds.Roll (PotionRewardOdds.cs:56-71): `float num4 = _rng.NextFloat(); if (flag || num4 < num3) ...` draws UNCONDITIONALLY before testing the force flag, so a forced drop (Hook.ShouldForcePotionReward, e.g. White Beast Statue) still consumes exactly one draw -- and rewards.py's PotionRewardOdds.roll (`hit = force or rolled`, evaluating `_uniform(self._rng)` first) preserves that non-short-circuit order. Boss-final-act early return matches run.py's `if room_type == RoomType.BOSS and run.is_final_act: apply_reward_modifiers(run, rewards); return rewards` (see step 15's dispatch-over-empty-list note, which is the same shape as this one).

steps.what: 2. TryGenerateTutorialRewards fork (RewardsSet.cs:258-327): gated on `player.UnlockState.NumberOfRuns == 0 && player.UnlockState.EpochUnlockCount() == 0 && player.Character is Ironclad` -- fixed, hand-picked card/potion/relic lists for the first 7 Monster fights, the first 2 Elites and the first Boss of a brand-new account, bypassing CardFactory/RelicFactory/PotionFactory entirely (no rarity roll, no upgrade roll, no bag pull).
steps.rationale: The sim's RunState models no fresh-account UnlockState (`rooms.py`'s own module docstring: "no unlock/epoch gating, no tutorial first-run '?' overrides" -- a pre-existing, already-declared scope boundary this seam inherits rather than re-derives). Every simulated run behaves as a returning player, so the C# gate's controlling predicate is unconditionally false in sim terms and the whole fork is unreachable. Not re-derived as a fresh finding; applying the existing convention to this file's own branch.

steps.what: 3. GenerateWithoutOffering's own re-entry guard: `if (_isGenerated) return;` (RewardsSet.cs:127-130), set true only at the very end (:146) -- makes the whole method safe to call twice.
steps.rationale: `CombatRewards.generated` (rewards.py) is the direct mirror, read at the top of `apply_reward_modifiers` and set at its tail, guarding the exact same double-call hazard the docstring explains (two real entry points into the same method -- see step 16).

steps.what: 4. `List<Reward> second = Rewards.ToList();` -- a snapshot of the pre-hook reward list, taken before the first populate loop, used only to detect hook-ADDED rewards later (RewardsSet.cs:131).
steps.rationale: The sim has no literal list-diff. `CombatRewards` is type-segregated (gold/potions/card_rewards/relics/special_cards/special_potions), and a hook-added `CardRewardGroup` is the ONLY reward-shaped thing a sim relic can add at generation time (`rewards.card_rewards.append(...)` from a `modify_combat_rewards[_late]` override) -- it is tracked with its own `populated: bool` flag (CardRewardGroup, rewards.py) rather than a before/after set difference. Functionally equivalent for every reward kind the sim's hook layer can actually add: a `CardRewardGroup` appended during either pass starts `populated=False` and is swept by step 8 exactly as an `Except(second)` member would be.

steps.what: 5. FIRST populate loop: `foreach (Reward reward in Rewards) reward.Populate();` over the list built in step 1, IN LIST ORDER -- Gold, then Potion (if rolled), then Card, then Relic (if Elite) (RewardsSet.cs:132-135).
steps.rationale: generate_combat_rewards's SP2-parity branch draws in exactly this order: `rewards.gold = roll_gold_reward(...)`, then (if got_potion) `rewards.potion = generate_random_potion(...)`, then `rewards.cards = create_reward_cards(...)`, then (Elite only) the relic rarity roll + bag pull. Per-subtype draw counts are steps 5a-5d.

steps.what: 5a. GoldReward.Populate: `Rng rng = _rngOverride ?? base.Player.PlayerRng.Rewards; Amount = rng.NextInt(_min, _max + 1);` -- exactly one draw, inclusive range (GoldReward.cs:69-73).
steps.rationale: roll_gold_reward (rewards.py) is `rng.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` on the parity Rewards stream (falling back to `randint(lo, hi)`, inclusive, on the legacy `random.Random` path) -- one draw, same half-open-to-inclusive transform. `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES` (10-20/35-45/100-100) matches `EncounterModel.MinGoldReward`/`MaxGoldReward`'s default room-type values; the Monster range is additionally scaled by `GoldProportion`, ported at rewards.py's `roll_gold_reward(..., proportion)` (RewardsSet.cs:227's `(int)Math.Round(... * combatRoom.GoldProportion)` vs `round(lo * proportion), round(hi * proportion)`).

steps.what: 5b. PotionReward.Populate: `Rng rng = _rngOverride ?? base.Player.PlayerRng.Rewards; Potion = PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat(base.Player, rng).ToMutable();` -- exactly one draw when the potion was NOT predetermined (PotionReward.cs:54-61); `CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat` itself is `CreateRandomPotion(options, 1, rng).First()`, one NextItem pick (PotionFactory.cs:31-34).
steps.rationale: `generate_random_potion(rew, pool=run.potion_pool)` (potion_pools.py, called from rewards.py) is one draw on the same rng argument passed through from generate_combat_rewards's `rew = run.rewards_rng`. Matches the one-draw shape; pool COMPOSITION is `relic_pools`'/`potion_pools`' own claim, not re-verdicted here.

steps.what: 5c. CardReward.Populate (not manually-set, not yet rerolled) delegates to `CardFactory.CreateForReward(player, OptionCount, cardCreationOptions)` -- OptionCount (3) cards, each: `Hook.ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions` (one call PER CARD, i.e. 3x total, CardFactory.cs:216) then a rarity roll (skipped entirely for CardRarityOddsType.Uniform, CardFactory.cs:219-224) then one `rng.NextItem(items)` pick (:236) then, unless NoUpgradeRoll is set, one unconditional upgrade draw whose OUTCOME is gated on IsUpgradable/Rarity/act index (RollForUpgrade, CardFactory.cs:283-305) -- so a normal 3-card reward spends 3 rarity rolls + 3 item picks + 3 upgrade draws = 9 draws on the Rewards stream, all on the SAME options object recomputed 3 times.
steps.rationale: create_reward_cards (rewards.py) reproduces every clause: the Uniform branch takes no rarity roll at all (`matching = options`, no `run.card_rarity_odds` call -- the module's own history notes a PRIOR bug here, since fixed, that burned an extra draw the game never takes); the upgrade draw is unconditional (`upgrade_roll = _uniform(rng)`) with the game's exact `NextFloat()`-before-guard shape, and is wholesale-skipped -- draw included -- under `NO_UPGRADE_ROLL`, matching `CardFactory.cs:98-102`'s guard sitting AROUND the draw rather than around only its effect. `Hook.ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions`'s per-card (3x) vs. the sim's once-before-the-loop dispatch is a distinct, separately-verdicted collapse -- see guard G1.

steps.what: 5d. RelicReward.Populate (Elite only, non-predetermined, no explicit rarity): `RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront(base.Player)` -> `RollRarity(player.PlayerRng.Rewards)` (one `NextFloat`, thresholds 0.5/0.83 for Common/Uncommon/Rare) then `player.RelicGrabBag.PullFromFront(rarity, filter, runState)` -- the bag pull itself takes NO further draw (RelicFactory.cs:26-49, 80-94).
steps.rationale: `roll_relic_rarity(rew)` (run.py) draws once on the same stream with the same 0.5/0.83 thresholds, then `run.pull_relic_from_front(rarity=rarity)` -- the sim's own comment states the bag pull "consumes none", matching `RelicGrabBag.PullFromFront`'s absence of any `Rng` parameter. Bag COMPOSITION/refill is `relic_pools`' claim; this seam verdicts only that the request is one rarity draw plus a draw-free pull.

steps.what: 5e. SpecialCardReward.Populate and CardRemovalReward.Populate are both empty method bodies -- no draw, no state (SpecialCardReward.cs:82-84; CardRemovalReward.cs:32-34). LinkedRewardSet.Populate delegates to its children in list order (LinkedRewardSet.cs:40-46).
steps.rationale: `SpecialCardReward`/`CardRemovalReward` have no sim class at all, and `LinkedRewardSet` is never constructed anywhere in `src/Core` (exhaustive grep of the whole game tree for `new LinkedRewardSet(` returns zero hits -- only the class body, the UI renderer `NLinkedRewardSet`, `NRewardsScreen`'s display branch and `Reward.ParentRewardSet`'s plumbing reference it). Both are unreachable: SpecialCardReward/CardRemovalReward's own reward-GRANT semantics are `special_cards`/an implicit run-level card-removal offer in the sim's `CombatRewards`/driver (draw-free on both sides, matching); LinkedRewardSet's grouping concept has no live C# call site to diverge from. If a future patch adds a `new LinkedRewardSet(...)` site, this waiver needs re-examination, not renewal.

steps.what: 6. `Hook.ModifyRewards(RunState, Player, Rewards, Room)` -- TWO complete passes over every hook listener: `TryModifyRewards` for all, THEN `TryModifyRewardsLate` for all, collecting everyone that returned true into `modifiers` (RewardsSet.cs:136; Hook.cs:1981-1999).
steps.rationale: `apply_reward_modifiers` (rewards.py) is `for relic in list(run.relics): relic.modify_combat_rewards(run, rewards)` THEN `for relic in list(run.relics): relic.modify_combat_rewards_late(run, rewards)` -- two complete walks, matching Hook.cs's two `foreach (AbstractModel item in runState.IterateHookListeners(null))` loops exactly (verified by reading Hook.cs:1981-1999 directly, not the sim's citation of it).

steps.what: 7. SECOND populate loop: `foreach (Reward item in Rewards.Except(second)) if (!item.IsPopulated) item.Populate();` -- ONLY rewards a hook added during step 6 get populated HERE, strictly after BOTH hook passes finished (RewardsSet.cs:137-143).
steps.rationale: `for group in rewards.card_rewards: if not group.populated: group.populate(run)` (apply_reward_modifiers tail, rewards.py) is the direct mirror, restricted to `CardRewardGroup` per step 4's rationale -- a Prayer Wheel-style extra card group added by either pass draws its options after the late pass has already run, matching C#'s ordering guarantee (the sim's own comment: "Prayer Wheel's three cards come off the Rewards stream behind everything the late pass did").

steps.what: 8. `await Hook.AfterModifyingRewards(Player.RunState, modifiers);` -- notifies ONLY the AbstractModels collected as `modifiers` across BOTH ModifyRewards passes, in hook-listener iteration order (RewardsSet.cs:144; Hook.cs:829-839).
steps.rationale: `Hook.AfterModifyingRewards` has exactly two C# overriders in the whole game (grep of `override.*AfterModifyingRewards` across src/): `AmethystAubergine.cs` and `WongosMysteryTicket.cs`. Both are already verdicted at the mechanism level by their own content records (`relic/amethyst_aubergine`: waiver, presentation-only `Flash()`; `relic/wongos_mystery_ticket`: faithful, "no separate counterpart; the sim performs the latch inline at the end of modify_combat_rewards"). Per rule 3 this seam matches rather than re-derives: the sim has no generic third dispatch pass, fusing each implementer's after-effect into its own modifying method instead -- verified correct for both of today's implementers by their own records. A FUTURE `AfterModifyingRewards` override that is NOT fused the same way would be this seam's blind spot, since nothing here re-checks the fusion generically.

steps.what: 9. `Rewards.Sort((x, y) => x.RewardsSetIndex.CompareTo(y.RewardsSetIndex));` -- re-orders the FLAT list for DISPLAY only (Gold=1, Potion=2, Relic=3, SpecialCard=4, Card=5, CardRemoval=7, LinkedRewardSet=max of its children; index 6 unused) (RewardsSet.cs:145; Reward.cs:39; each subtype's RewardsSetIndex override).
steps.rationale: This sort governs on-screen ordering only -- it runs AFTER every draw in steps 5-8 has already happened in INSERTION order (not display order), so it cannot affect RNG or hook dispatch, the seam's actual subject. The sim's `CombatRewards` is type-segregated fields (gold/potions/card_rewards/relics/special_cards/special_potions) rather than one flat sorted `List<Reward>`, so the grouping this sort exists to produce is achieved by construction instead of by a runtime sort. No content record depends on a literal `Rewards[]` index.

steps.what: 10. `RewardsSet.WithRewardsFromRoom` on a TreasureRoom: `GenerateRewardsFor`'s switch has NO `TreasureRoom` case (the type-check only distinguishes 'throw' from 'not throw', RewardsSet.cs:213-219), so the returned list -- and therefore `Rewards` -- is EMPTY. `TreasureRoom.cs:82` still calls `RewardsCmd.GenerateForRoomEnd`, so steps 3-9 above all run over that empty list, including `Hook.ModifyRewards` firing with `Room` set to the TreasureRoom.
steps.rationale: `run.py`'s TREASURE branch (`RoomType.TREASURE` arm of `_resolve_room_point`/`enter_point`) builds `treasure_rewards = CombatRewards(room_type=RoomType.MONSTER, room=RoomType.TREASURE)` and calls `apply_reward_modifiers(self, treasure_rewards)` on it directly -- an empty base CombatRewards, hooks dispatched anyway -- and the sim's own comment cites this exact C# shape (RewardsSet.cs:213-219, :136) by line number. The chest's own gold+relic grant (OneOffSynchronizer/TreasureRoomRelicSynchronizer -- NOT pinned to this seam, see the scope note below) is a wholly separate mechanism that never goes through RewardsSet at all; this step verdicts only that RewardsSet's OWN empty-list-plus-hook-dispatch shape for a TreasureRoom is reproduced, which it is.

steps.what: 11. Two independent call sites reach `GenerateWithoutOffering` (steps 3-9): GENERATE-time, via `RewardsCmd.GenerateForRoomEnd` (every CombatRoom/TreasureRoom, called BEFORE the room ever offers anything -- CombatRoom.cs:267, TreasureRoom.cs:82); and OFFER-time, via `RewardsSet.Offer()`'s own call at RewardsSet.cs:159, which is the ONLY dispatch for every `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom` set (rest-site heals, 13+ events, 8+ relics) since those never call GenerateForRoomEnd first. Step 3's `_isGenerated` guard is what makes calling it from both a no-op for the first kind and the ONLY firing for the second.
steps.rationale: The sim mirrors both entry points by design (rewards.py's own extensive module-level docstring on `apply_reward_modifiers`, itself verified against Hook.cs and RewardsCmd.cs by this audit rather than trusted): construction sites call `apply_reward_modifiers` explicitly (mirroring generate-time), and `driver._offer_rewards`/`RunState.offer_rewards` call it again as an idempotent backstop (mirroring offer-time) -- guarded by the same `generated`/`_isGenerated` flag from step 3, so a future site that forgets the explicit call still fires exactly once rather than silently skipping every reward-modifying relic.

steps.what: 12. `Offer()`: re-calls `GenerateWithoutOffering()` (a no-op for a generate-time set per step 11); bails with nothing shown if `Rewards.Count <= 0 && Room is not CombatRoom && !_allowEmptyRewards`; otherwise shows the screen, or in TestMode auto-selects every reward in list order via `_synchronizer.SelectLocalReward` (RewardsSet.cs:153-196).
steps.rationale: `CombatRewards.is_empty` (rewards.py) is the direct analogue of the bail predicate (gold==0, no potions, no cards in any group, no relics, no special cards/potions); the sim's driver resolves each field as a decision rather than auto-selecting in TestMode's sense, which is the presentation/interaction-flow half already declared out of scope by the shared contract (no UI, synchronous driver).

steps.what: 13. `Reward.SelectUnsynchronized`: `OnSelect()` -> on success, `Hook.AfterRewardTaken(RunState, Player, this)` fires ONCE per accepted reward, immediately, not batched (Reward.cs:120-134; Hook.cs:1092-1099).
steps.rationale: `Hook.AfterRewardTaken` has ZERO overriding implementers anywhere in `src/` (grep of `override.*AfterRewardTaken` / `virtual.*AfterRewardTaken` across the whole game tree returns only the one `virtual` no-op declaration on `AbstractModel.cs:1106`). Unreachable by construction -- no content exists to diverge from. Re-examine if a future patch adds the first implementer.

steps.what: 14. OnSkipped semantics (decline path), per subtype: CardReward/SpecialCardReward log each un-picked option to `CurrentMapPointHistoryEntry` history and do nothing else; RelicReward/PotionReward, if `!_wasTaken`, log to history only -- the relic/potion was already PULLED from its bag/pool during step 5, so a decline never returns the draw or the pulled instance to the pool (Reward.cs; CardReward.cs:313-320; RelicReward.cs:117-123; PotionReward.cs:95-101). `RewardsSet.WithSkippingDisallowed` / `_disallowSkipping` forces every reward to be taken before the screen dismisses; its ONE caller in the whole game is `NeowsBones.cs:43`.
steps.rationale: None of C#'s four OnSkipped bodies consume RNG or reverse a prior draw -- decline is bookkeeping-only on both sides. The sim's own comments make the no-refund property explicit at every relevant call site: `run.offer_relic`'s docstring states "RelicReward.Populate has already run by then -- a declined relic still LEAVES the grab bag", and `generate_combat_rewards`'s Elite branch comment repeats it ("the pull already happened in Populate, so a decline still spends the bag slot"). `WithSkippingDisallowed`/`_disallowSkipping` has no sim counterpart at all (grep of `disallow_skipping`/`DisallowSkipping` returns nothing under sts2_rl/), but its only observable effect is forcing a screen-dismissal DECISION before leaving -- a presentation/interaction-flow constraint with no effect on generation order, draw count, or hook dispatch (this seam's subject). Whether `relic/neows_bones`'s own port needs to force its driver-side decision to match is that content record's question, not re-derived here.

steps.what: 15. `LinkedRewardSet.OnSelect` cascades: `Reward.SelectUnsynchronized`, on success, calls `ParentRewardSet.RemoveReward(this)` then `await ParentRewardSet.OnSelect()` -- claiming one linked child removes it and re-checks the group (Reward.cs:128-132; LinkedRewardSet.cs:48-56).
steps.rationale: Carries step 5e's waiver: `LinkedRewardSet` is never constructed anywhere in `src/Core`, so this cascade is dead code in the current build and there is nothing for the sim (which has no LinkedRewardSet concept) to diverge from.

steps.what: 16. `CardReward`'s constructor subscribes `player.RelicObtained += OnRelicObtained` and stays subscribed for the whole time the reward is unclaimed (unsubscribed only in `OnSelect`'s tail or `OnSkipped`); `OnRelicObtained` re-runs BOTH `TryModifyCardRewardOptions`/`Late` for JUST the newly-obtained relic against the STILL-PENDING `_cards`, retroactively upgrading/enchanting/removing already-generated card options (CardReward.cs:117, 167-181, 293, 319).
steps.issue: The sim has no counterpart: grep of `RelicObtained`/`OnRelicObtained` returns nothing under sts2_rl/. This exact mechanism was already found and verdicted DORMANT by `relic/silver_crucible`'s `AfterModifyingCardRewardOptions` hook entry (2026-07-26, round 6): "CardReward.OnRelicObtained ... re-runs both modifier hooks when a relic is obtained while a reward screen is open ... That path is dormant (the sim grants relics between rooms, never with a reward screen open)". Matched here per rule 3 rather than re-derived. FLAGGED, not overturned: this seam's own read of `generate_combat_rewards`'s Elite branch (rewards.py) shows `rewards.cards = create_reward_cards(...)` completing BEFORE `run.offer_relic(relic)` resolves that SAME elite's own relic reward, inside the SAME function call -- i.e. a relic IS obtained while that elite's own CardRewardGroup already holds drawn-but-still-unclaimed cards, which reads as narrower than "between rooms" for this one case. Reported as a possible staleness in the cited record's dormancy premise, not as a contradicting verdict: confirming it live requires a specific Common/Uncommon relic that (a) is reachable via an Elite's own grab-bag pull and (b) implements `modify_card_reward_options[_late]` against already-drawn cards, which is `relic_pools`'/content-tier's determination, not re-derived here.

steps.what: 17. `Hook.ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions` (CardFactory.cs:216) is dispatched ONCE PER CARD inside `CardFactory`'s private per-card `CreateForReward` (called `OptionCount` times, i.e. 3x for a normal reward) -- not once per whole reward.
steps.rationale: `create_reward_cards` (rewards.py) computes the widened pool ONCE, before its per-card loop, and reuses it for all `count` iterations -- collapsing 3 C# dispatches into 1. Verified safe against the CURRENT roster, not assumed: the only two Ironclad-reachable, currently-ported implementers of this hook are `DingyRug.cs`/`dingy_rug.py` and `PrismaticGem.cs` (unported) -- both are pure functions of the input `options` with no counter/state mutation (read in full: `PrismaticGem.cs:28-41` returns early on owner/flag checks or appends a fixed pool, nothing else), so firing 3 times vs. 1 time yields the IDENTICAL widened pool every time. `CharacterCards.cs`/`BigGameHunter.cs` are the two other C# implementers and are Custom/Daily-mode `Modifiers`, out of the Ironclad-only sim's scope. A FUTURE stateful implementer (a per-call counter, a one-shot latch) would silently break this collapse -- flagged as fragility, not as a present divergence.

steps.what: 18. `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions` (CardFactory.cs:106, dispatched from the per-reward `CreateForReward(player, cardCount, options)` AFTER the per-card loop, gated on `!options.Flags.HasFlag(NoModifyHooks)`) is ALSO a two-complete-pass dispatch: every relic's plain hook, then every relic's Late hook (Hook.cs:1445-1467).
steps.rationale: `create_reward_cards`'s tail (rewards.py) runs `for relic in list(run.relics): relic.modify_card_reward_options(...)` THEN `for relic in list(run.relics): relic.modify_card_reward_options_late(...)`, matching the two complete C# passes read directly from Hook.cs:1445-1467 (not from the sim's own citation of it). This is the SAME two-pass shape as step 6, at a different call site.

guards.what: G1 (rarity-ladder ports): CardRarityOddsType's five base-odds tuples (Regular 0.03/0.37/0.60, Elite 0.10/0.40/0.50, Boss 1/0/0, Shop 0.09/0.37/0.54, Uniform 0.33/0.33/0.33 -- non-ascension values) and the drifting pity offset (base -0.05, growth +0.01, cap +0.40, reset to -0.05 on a Rare; Boss rolls use offset 0 but still reset the counter; shops read via RollWithoutChangingFutureOdds without mutating).
guards.rationale: Read `CardRarityOdds.cs` (Odds/) end to end against `rewards.py`'s `CardRarityOdds` class: every constant, every threshold comparison (`num < num2` for Rare, `num < GetBaseOdds(Uncommon) + num2` for Uncommon) and the post-roll mutation (`Roll` resets to -0.05 on Rare, else `Min(current + growth, 0.4)`) match the sim's `roll`/`roll_without_changing_future_odds`/`roll_with_base_odds` trio exactly, including `roll_with_base_odds`'s documented quirk (compares against the RAW uncommon band, not rare+uncommon) which the sim's own comment flags and preserves rather than 'fixes'.

guards.what: G2: WHICH roll method (mutating `Roll` vs. non-mutating `RollWithBaseOdds`) is selected -- C#'s actual predicate is `forceRarityOddsChange || (source == Encounter && rollMethod in {Regular, Elite, Boss})` (CardFactory.cs:244-260's `RollForRarity`), not simply `source == Encounter` as `create_reward_cards`'s `mutate_pity` parameter implies.
guards.rationale: Verified by exhaustive grep: `CardCreationSource.Encounter` is constructed at exactly two places in the whole game (`CardCreationOptions.ForRoom`, and RewardsSet's tutorial-reward constructor which itself always passes `CardCreationOptions.ForRoom(...)` as `rerollOptions`) -- and `ForRoom`'s switch pairs `Encounter` ONLY with `RegularEncounter`/`EliteEncounter`/`BossEncounter`, never `Shop`/`Uniform`. So `source == Encounter` and `rollMethod in {Regular,Elite,Boss}` are provably co-extensive today, and the sim's simpler `mutate_pity = (source == Encounter)` heuristic (`CardRewardGroup._mutate_pity`) is equivalent, not merely lucky. `forceRarityOddsChange` is a SEPARATE bypass with exactly one C# setter in the whole game -- `SealedDeck.cs:30`, a Custom/Daily-mode `Modifier` -- so it is dead in Ironclad-only scope; the sim has no `FORCE_RARITY_ODDS_CHANGE` reader, which is correctly unreachable rather than missing.

guards.what: G3: `CardCreationFlags`'s combo values -- `NoUpgrades = 6` (`NoUpgradeRoll | NoHookUpgrades`) and `NoModifications = -1` (all 32 bits) -- have no named counterpart in `rewards.py`'s `IntFlag` port.
guards.rationale: Grep of `NoUpgrades`/`NoModifications` (and their sim-cased forms) across the WHOLE game tree returns zero references anywhere OTHER than the enum declaration itself -- no C# call site constructs either combo by name. The sim's 8 individual bit values (1,2,4,8,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x80) match the C# ones exactly, so ANY combination -- named or not -- is preserved bit-for-bit by Python `IntFlag`'s OR arithmetic; a named alias is documentation, not semantics, and the sim's `IntFlag` needs no such alias to reproduce either combo's bit pattern if a future caller ever OR's the individual flags together.

guards.what: G4: `CardCreationFlags.NoRarityModification`'s only C# reader is `BigGameHunter.cs:40` (`options.Flags.HasFlag(NoCardPoolModifications) || options.Flags.HasFlag(NoRarityModification)`), and `NoCardModelModifications` has zero C# readers anywhere.
guards.rationale: `BigGameHunter` is a Custom/Daily-mode `Modifier` (same family as `SealedDeck`), out of the Ironclad-only sim's scope -- the ONLY reader of `NoRarityModification` is unreachable, and `NoCardModelModifications` has no reader at all to diverge from. The sim's own comment (`rewards.py`'s `CardCreationFlags` docstring) independently reaches the same conclusion ("have no ported reader yet"), verified here against the C# rather than trusted from the comment per PROMPT.md's calibration rule on docstrings.

guards.what: G5: reward card pool scope -- `CardCreationOptions.GetPossibleCards` == `CardPoolModel.GetUnlockedCards` (`FilterThroughEpochs` + multiplayer-constraint filter ONLY -- no Basic/Ancient/CanBeGeneratedInCombat exclusion), NOT `CardFactory.FilterForCombat`'s combat-only filter.
